content.rendered: Thanks for this list! I amost forgot about some of these. One category that might be worth adding is the Marriott cards. I know there’s an airline credit this year, and some kind of annual spending threshold on the Chase boundless card

As we all close out the year and chase our last remaining credits, let’s all give a big thanks to William and the rest of the staff for keeping this site running and focused. It’s certainly no easy feat, and it’s certainly been great seeing DoC stay focused and true to it’s mission for all these years. I’m certain anyone reading this far into the comments could point to a dozen other sites that, whilst once great resources, devolved into affiliate-link infested, AI-article-infested SEO optimized shells of what they once were.

I’ll throw a last shout-out to DoC’s charity partner, Cure Alzheimer’s Fund. Donation link is at the bottom right, and for the 2026 tax year even those taking the standard deduction can deduct up to $1k ($2k if filing jointly) in charitable contributions.
Also the time where I add up all the money I netted YTD, definitely a grand thanks to DoC and the ones providing data points

Additional, under “Calendar Year Spend Requirements”

  • Chase Sapphire reserve: Spend $75k, get IHG Diamond, Southwest Silver, $500 Southwest Credit (via Chase Travel), $250 The Shops at Chase Credit
  • Cap1 Venture X: Spend $75k, get extra Capital One lounge guests
I don’t believe I see the 10k mile annual mile bonus (by card member year) for the United Quest card.
Amex referral limits are 5 per card now, not limited by points.
We have the CSR. Added the Cap1. Thanks
Added the marriott $50 temporary credit. The other spending threshold I don’t think it ever resets, it just keeps accumulating, so I”ll leave that out. Thank you
